query_tables.title: List the account's tables
query_tables.description: Every table in the storage account, each as `{"TableName": "..."}`. Page with the `x-ms-continuation-NextTableName` header the response carries -- which this package does not surface, so a very large account may need `$top` and a filter instead.

filter.description: OData filter over table names, e.g. "TableName ge 'orders'".

accept.description: OData metadata level. nometadata keeps the response clean.

create_table.title: Create a table
create_table.description:
Create a table in the account. Table names are 3 to 63 alphanumeric characters, must start with a letter, and are case-insensitive for uniqueness but case-sensitive in URLs -- so create `Orders` and address it as `Orders`, not `orders`.
Fails with 409 if the table already exists.

table_name.description: The table name -- 3 to 63 alphanumeric characters, starting with a letter.

delete_table.title: Delete a table
delete_table.description:
Destroy a table and every entity in it. Irreversible -- Table Storage has no soft delete.
The name stays unusable for at least 40 seconds afterwards while the service finishes the delete, so an immediate recreate returns 409.
delete_table.notes: Deletes every entity. The name cannot be reused for about 40 seconds.

table_name.description: The table to destroy, with every entity in it.

get_table_acl.title: Get a table's stored access policies
get_table_acl.description: The stored access policies on a table, as XML. A shared access signature bound to one of these can be revoked by deleting the policy; a free-standing SAS cannot be revoked at all short of rotating the account key. An empty document means every SAS on this table is of the second kind.

output.description: An XML SignedIdentifiers document, empty when no policies are set.

query_entities.title: Query entities in a table
query_entities.description:
Read entities from a table, optionally filtered and projected.
Performance is decided entirely by the filter. `PartitionKey eq 'acme' and RowKey eq '1001'` is a point read. `PartitionKey eq 'acme'` scans one partition. Anything else -- `Status eq 'open'`, `Amount gt 100` -- scans the WHOLE TABLE, because Table Storage has no secondary indexes. That works on a small table and degrades without warning as it grows.
`$select` cuts the properties returned, which is worth doing on wide entities. `$top` caps the page at up to 1000; the continuation tokens for the next page come back as `x-ms-continuation-*` response headers, which this package does not surface, so treat `$top` as a limit rather than as paging.
query_entities.notes: A filter that does not name PartitionKey scans the entire table. There are no secondary indexes.

filter.description: OData filter. Name PartitionKey to keep it fast, e.g. "PartitionKey eq 'acme' and Status eq 'open'".

select.description: Comma-separated property names to return, e.g. "RowKey,Status,Amount".

top.description: Maximum entities to return, up to 1000.

accept.description: OData metadata level. nometadata keeps the response clean; fullmetadata includes property types.

items.description: Each entity's PartitionKey, RowKey, Timestamp and its own properties.

get_entity.title: Read one entity by its keys
get_entity.description:
Point-read a single entity by `PartitionKey` and `RowKey`. The fastest and cheapest operation Table Storage offers -- always prefer it to query_entities when both keys are known.
Returns 404 when no entity has that key pair. Use `application/json;odata=minimalmetadata` as the accept level if you need the `odata.etag` for a subsequent conditional update, since nometadata omits it.
get_entity.notes: nometadata omits odata.etag; use minimalmetadata when you need the etag for update_entity.

accept.description: OData metadata level. minimalmetadata includes odata.etag.

output.description: The entity, or 404 when the key pair matches nothing.

insert_entity.title: Insert a new entity
insert_entity.description:
Add an entity to a table. The body must carry `PartitionKey` and `RowKey` as strings; every other property is yours.
Types beyond string, double and bool need an OData hint alongside the value: `{"Created": "2026-01-15T00:00:00Z", "Created@odata.type": "Edm.DateTime"}`. Without it a timestamp is stored as a string and will not compare correctly in a filter.
Fails with 409 if that key pair already exists -- use insert_or_replace_entity when you want an upsert instead.
insert_entity.notes: Fails with 409 on a duplicate key pair. Non-string types need an @odata.type hint.

entity.description: The entity, including PartitionKey and RowKey as strings, plus any @odata.type hints for typed properties.

prefer.description: return-no-content gives a 204 with an empty body; return-content echoes the stored entity back.

output.description: The entity as stored, when return-content was asked for.

update_entity.title: Replace an existing entity
update_entity.description:
Overwrite an entity with the body you send. This REPLACES: any property not in `entity` is removed from the stored entity. Merge is not reachable through this connector, so read the entity with get_entity, change what you need and send the whole thing back.
`if_match` is required. Pass the entity's `odata.etag` for an optimistic update that fails with 412 if it changed since you read it -- which is how you avoid silently discarding a concurrent write -- or `*` to overwrite whatever is there.
update_entity.notes: A full replace, not a merge. Properties omitted from the body are deleted.

entity.description: The complete replacement entity, including PartitionKey and RowKey. Anything omitted is removed.

if_match.description: The entity's odata.etag for a conditional update, or "*" to overwrite unconditionally.

output.description: Empty on success (204); 412 when the etag did not match.

insert_or_replace_entity.title: Upsert an entity
insert_or_replace_entity.description:
Insert an entity, or replace it entirely if that key pair already exists. Idempotent, which makes it the right tool for syncing external records into a table -- insert_entity would fail on the second run.
As with update_entity this REPLACES rather than merges: properties absent from the body are not carried over from the existing entity. There is no concurrency check, by design.
insert_or_replace_entity.notes: Replaces the whole entity. No etag check, so a concurrent write is overwritten without warning.

entity.description: The complete entity, including PartitionKey and RowKey. Becomes the whole stored entity.

delete_entity.title: Delete an entity
delete_entity.description:
Remove one entity. Irreversible -- there is no recycle bin.
`if_match` is required: the entity's `odata.etag` makes the delete conditional and fails with 412 if it changed since you read it, and `*` deletes unconditionally.

if_match.description: The entity's odata.etag for a conditional delete, or "*" to delete unconditionally.

output.description: Empty on success (204); 412 when the etag did not match.

get_service_properties.title: Get the table service's logging and metrics settings
get_service_properties.description: The account-wide Table Storage configuration as XML: analytics logging, hour and minute metrics, and CORS rules. Read it when you need to know whether table operations are being logged before trying to audit them.

get_service_stats.title: Get geo-replication status for the table service
get_service_stats.description: Replication status and last sync time for the secondary region. Only answers on the secondary endpoint of a read-access geo-redundant account. `LastSyncTime` marks how far the secondary has caught up -- writes after it may not be readable there yet.
get_service_stats.notes: Only valid against the secondary endpoint of an RA-GRS account. Returns XML.

output.description: An XML StorageServiceStats document with the geo-replication status and last sync time.
